title: Swiggy board approves Rs 10,000 Cr fundraise
passage: Swiggy Limited's board approved on November 7, 2025 a plan to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore (~$1.13 billion) through equity via a qualified institutional placement (QIP) or other permissible routes, in one or more tranches, subject to shareholder approval. Stated purpose: to strengthen its balance sheet and fuel growth across its core food delivery business and quick-commerce arm, Instamart. The move follows Swiggy reporting a widened Q2 FY26 loss of Rs 1,092 crore, and mirrors competitor Zomato's earlier Rs 8,500 crore QIP.

title: Orders under Section 26(1) of the Act: CCI Directs Investigation Against Zomato and Swiggy
passage: On April 4, 2022, in Case No. 16 of 2021, the Competition Commission of India (CCI) directed an investigation into Zomato and Swiggy under Section 26(1) of the Competition Act, 2002, following a complaint by the National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI). NRAI alleged coerced bundling of listing and delivery services, data masking creating conflicts of interest with the platforms' own private labels/cloud kitchens, one-sided contract termination clauses, price-parity mandates, exclusivity requirements, high commissions, and deep discounting. The CCI directed investigation specifically into price-parity and exclusivity practices and potential conflicts of interest from private-label operations; it found bundling, delayed payments, one-sided clauses and commission levels not to warrant further investigation at that stage.

title: Swiggy (Wikipedia)
passage: Swiggy was incorporated on 26 December 2013 by Sriharsha Majety, Nandan Reddy and Rahul Jaimini, and launched its food delivery service in August 2014. Headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. Swiggy operates as an online food ordering and delivery company and also provides quick-commerce services under the name Instamart. As of 2025, it serves more than 700 Indian cities for food delivery and 100 cities for quick-commerce. It became a unicorn by 2018. Swiggy launched its initial public offering (IPO) in November 2024 at Rs 390 (US$4.00) per share, valuing the company at $11.3 billion.

title: Exclusive-India Finds Zomato, Swiggy Food Delivery Businesses Breached Antitrust Laws, Documents Show
passage: India's antitrust investigation arm found that Zomato's and Swiggy's food delivery businesses breached competition law by favouring select restaurant partners, including through exclusivity arrangements that guaranteed business growth to restaurants listing exclusively on one platform. The investigation arm's report said such exclusivity arrangements prevent the market from becoming more competitive. Karnataka High Court subsequently granted interim protection to Swiggy against the CCI proceedings, with the stay later extended to a hearing scheduled for April 25, 2026.

title: Swiggy Q4 FY25 Results Press Release
passage: Bengaluru, India, May 9, 2025. Swiggy (Swiggy Ltd, NSE: SWIGGY / BSE: 544285) reported results for the quarter and full year ended March 31, 2025. Platform Gross Order Value (B2C GOV) rose ~40% YoY to INR 12,888 Cr; Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA loss was INR 732 Cr. Food delivery GOV grew 17.6% YoY to INR 7,347 Cr; Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 2.9% of GOV (from 0.5% a year ago). Instamart GOV grew 101% YoY to INR 4,670 Cr in Q4, added 316 darkstores in the quarter, expanded to 124 cities; Adjusted EBITDA loss increased to INR 840 Cr. Platform Average MTU grew 35% YoY to 19.8 million. About Swiggy: founded 2014, enabled by 5.4 lakh delivery partners, Swiggy Food collaborates with over 2.5 lakh restaurants across ~700 cities, Swiggy Instamart operates in 120+ cities. Legal entity: Swiggy Limited, formerly 'Swiggy Private Limited' and 'Bundl Technologies Private Limited', CIN U74110KA2013PLC096530.
